svg.text: SparkFun Pro nRF52840 Mini. Flames: 2N3904 low-side switches. RGB core (common cathode): 2N3906 high-side switches. All LEDs fed from the board's 3V3 pin. Yellow tags are net names: same name = same wire.
top view, USB and JST at the top
BAT+ / BAT- pads sit beside the JST
Yellow pins are the only ones we use. Pin numbers are the header labels (P0.xx).
10 mm diffused RGB LED, common cathode (4 legs, longest = common)
common cathode straight to GND; the PNPs switch the anodes
Reads half the cell voltage; the firmware doubles it. Without it the
firmware reports "battery not connected" and simply skips the cutoff.
If you ever swap in a common-ANODE RGB LED
wire its three elements exactly like the flame channels (2N3904 low side, common leg to 3V3)
and set the three rgb channels back to PWM_POLARITY_NORMAL in app.overlay.
Why the PNP for common cathode: an NPN above the LED can only reach the pin voltage
minus 0.7 V, about 2.6 V, which lights red but not green or blue. The PNP's emitter sits
on 3V3, so the element gets the full rail minus about 0.15 V, the same as the flames.
PNP logic is inverted: pin LOW = element on. The firmware handles that (inverted PWM),
and the 10 k pull-up keeps the core dark while the pins float during reset or bootloader.
Direct drive from the pins was the fallback: no parts, but 5 mA max per pin and almost no
headroom for green and blue, so a dim, red-tinted core.
2N3904 and 2N3906: flat face toward you, legs E B C from left to right.
Flame channels (NPN): 1 k pin to base, 100 k base to GND, emitter to GND,
LED string from 3V3 into the collector. Pin high = LED on.
RGB channels (PNP): emitter to 3V3, 1 k pin to base, 10 k base to 3V3,
collector through the resistor into the element anode. Pin low = on.
One series resistor per LED, never shared between LEDs:
5 mm amber / yellow / red: 100 R (about 11 mA each)
mini LEDs in the cluster: 220 R each (about 5 mA each, 3 to 6 LEDs)
RGB red element: 100 R. RGB green and blue elements: 20 R (10 R if too dim)
All LEDs hang off the board's 3V3 pin, so the power switch cuts them too.
Everything on at full brightness is about 120 mA; the 3V3 regulator gives 600 mA.
The pins are plain outputs: a miswired channel just stays dark. Only connecting
3V3, VIN or a battery pad straight to a signal pin could hurt the board.
